Cabot City Council Agenda Meeting
Cabot City Annex / Council Chambers
January 5, 2015
6:30 p.m.

The Cabot City Council held its monthly Agenda Meeting on January 5, 2015 in the City Annex Council
Chambers. Council members Present were: Ann Gilliam, Ed Long, Doyle Tullos, Dallan Buchanan, Ronald
Waymack, Kevin Davis, Jon Moore and Rick Prentice. Others present: Mayor Cypert, City Attorney Jim Taylor,
City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom, Calvin Aldridge, CPA, & Eddie Cook.

Ed Long, Chairman of the Public Works Committee called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.
Public Works:

1. Accept Bid for Central Detention Pond — Brain Boroughs explained this has been an ongoing
plan for two to three years; flash flooding is a big problem in the area, there is already a berm
designed to keep water off certain properties. This project will take water from the basin and
redirect it to the detention pond which will store it temporarily and release it at a much slower
flow to prevent flash flooding along Pear Street to Spence Street. We have obtained a 50/50
grant up to $75,000 which was in the budget adopted for 2015, and the project must be
complete by May 1" for the grant. Reynolds was the lowest bidder with a $105,600 bid coming
in under estimate. Motion to place item on the council meeting’s agenda by Ann, second by
Jon. Motion passed. Doyle asked if a performance bond was required. Brian Boroughs stated
the contractor is required to provide a bond. Detailed information provided by Whitlow
Engineering Services, Inc. regarding the Detention Basin at Central Elementary School is
attached to these minutes.

Public Works Community Input - Deborah Moore, Regional Library Director addressed the council members.
Please see attached for the information she provided. Mayor Cypert explained the Lonoke/Prairie County
Regional Library System operates the library and the City owns the building and the improvements being made
to it are paid out of the 2013 Bond Issue; the City is well pleased with what they do and how they do it.

Budget & Personnet: (Ann Gilliam)

1. Appoint Ann Gilliam to A&P Commission — Mayor Cypert spoke to items 1,2 & 3. He pointed
out the Advertising & Promotion Commission is a statutory commission sanctioned by Ark. Code
Ann. § 26-75-605 with its operation being endorsed by City Ordinance 6 of 2009. He continued, it
shall consist of seven (7} members. Four (4) members shall be owners or managers of businesses in
the tourism industry, at least three (3) of whom shall be owners or managers of hotels, motels, or
restaurants and shatl be appointed by the remaining members with approval by the city council.
Two (2} members shall be members of the governing body. Mayor Cypert reminded the council of
the December's Agenda meeting when they were asked and in agreement with Ed and Ann
continuing to serve on the commission, thus the reason for them being presented. Mayor Cypert
continued, one (1) member shall be from the public at large and shall be appointed by the remaining
members with approval from the city council. Mayor Cypert named Mr. Tommy Hignight as the
commission’s recommendation as per their meeting minutes. Mr. Hignight was recognized by the
Commission Chair, and given an opportunity to speak and answer questions. There were no

--- page 2 (OCR) ---
questions or comments. Vice-Chair Jon was in agreement with Jimmy Taylor that it is appropriate to
make a motion including all 3 items vs each item individually. Motion to place items 1, 2, & 3 on the
council meeting’s agenda by Kevin, second by Ronald. Vice-Chair Jon called for the vote. Ann Gilliam
and Ed Long both abstained from voting on this motion. Motion passed.

Procedure for Committee/Agenda Process — Mayor Cypert declared the city has two obsolete
ordinances (3 of 2007 and 6 of 2011) and this item replaces both of those with protocol that
emulates and stipulates the very successful process we are going through now. Motion to place
item on the council meeting’s agenda by Jon, second by Dallan. Motion passed.

Council Committee Appointments - Motion by Jon to place resolution appointing council
members to committees on the council meeting’s agenda, second by Dallan. Motion passed.
Recording of the Elected Officials with the County Clerk ~ Mayor Cypert presented this item as in
compliance with House Bill 1314 of 2013. Motion to place item on the council meeting’s agenda
by Rick, second by Dallan. Motion passed.

Review of the 2013 Audit — Calvin Aldridge, CPA partner with Ellis, Tucker & Aldridge, LLP who
serves as a consultant to the city, summarized the opinions and findings of the Legislative Joint
Auditing Committee included in their audit for year 2013. In his report to the Council, he offered
the following: this audit covers General Fund, Street Fund and certain other funds, but not
Water & Wastewater, A&P, or Parks and Recreation. Financial statements are prepared on a
Regulatory Basis deemed to be acceptable by the state of Arkansas, but not in accordance with
Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP). Calvin explained that many other Arkansas
cities, counties, and state government agencies’ financials are done in accordance with Arkansas
code and not GAAP. He established the primary purpose of an audit is to express an opinion that
the Financial Statements are fairly stated in all material respects, report on internal controls, and
to identify any non-compliance with laws, regulations, grant agreements, and any matters that
come to their attention that are material to the amounts reported within the Financial
Statements. Calvin indicated the most important opinion is found on page 2, paragraph 4 which
states “in our opinion, except for the omission of the information described in the “Basis for
Qualified Opinions on Regulatory Basis of Accounting” paragraph, the financial statements
referred to above present fairly, in all material respects, the regulatory basis financial position of
the general fund and street fund of the City of Cabot, as of December 31, 2013, and the
regulatory basis revenues, expenditures, and changes in net position, and the budgetary
comparisons for the general fund and street fund for the year then ended in accordance with the
financial reporting provisions of the Arkansas Code described in Note 1.” The omission of
required disclosures regarding deposit risks has been a part of the history of Cabot’s audits due
largely to the many different funds and commissions that handle them. However, the goal is to
get this comment removed next year if at all possible. He continued with an opinion on page 3,
#2013-1 which details a deficiency in internal control regarding segregation of duties. Again, it
was explained this finding is a yearly occurrence that is attributed to limited financial resources
of the City. The response by the Clerk/Treasurer, District Court Clerk, and Police Chief agreed to
segregate their offices to the extent possible as recommended. The next opinion mentioned is
on page 4, paragraph 1 which states “The results of our tests disclosed no instances of
noncompliance or other matters that are required to be reported under Government Auditing

--- page 3 (OCR) ---
Standards.” Calvin voiced his approval of this kind of finding. Further down on page 4, the audit
indicates the City is in substantial compliance with Arkansas fiscal and financial laws concerning
general and district court accounting, budgeting, purchasing and investing and depositing of
public funds. A noncompliance issue regarding the Disaster Recovery Plan was found requiring
the City to do some long term planning for interruptions of computer processing. Calvin
declared this to be a good report, one of the best he’s seen in past years. There were no
questions or comments and no action needed by the council.

8. Financials: No questions

9. Budget & Personne! Community Input - NONE

2. Monthly Reports — Fire Department-see reports. Police and Fire Community Input- None

members the following week vs meeting after the Agenda Meeting and having to wait 30 days for the next

Agenda Meeting.

Thank you for the opportunity to address the Cabot Agenda Committee on Monday, January 5
at the city annex.

The new Cabot Library is progressing on time and smoothly. We are at 68% completion. The
brick has been installed on the exterior and the ceilings are being painted on the inside. All
interior colors have been chosen; the shelving units and furnishings have been chosen and
ordered. Our staff will begin their training on “packing and moving the current library to its
new location” in the February staff meeting. This will be quite the undertaking but the staff is
anxious to be in the new building as we know we can better serve our patrons and our
community. We hope to be closed only 2-3 weeks for our move. The target date for the
opening will be late May or early June of this year.

The Community Meeting Room of the new library will be a large draw for civic club use and
educational endeavors as well as our 2 pod areas. We will have a large circulation desk that will
accommodate 2-3 “seif-check outs” as well as circulation staff and hopefully facilitate the
circulation of materials in a more organized and timely fashion.

We know we are having an impact in the “library world” as it was quoted in the newspaper
recently that “Sherwood is contemplating remodeling a grocery store to accommodate their
new library—like the Cabot library is currently doing”.

Again we would like to thank Dayco Construction, Bill Kennedy (job superintendent), and
Schelle Architects for making this construction remodel endeavor a smooth and painless one
(on time and on budget). We want to thank the Mayor of Cabot, Bill Cypert, the Cabot City
Council and the voters of Cabot for making this dream a reality. You are invited to come and
take a tour of the facility any day between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.

Thank you.

Deborah Moore
Regional Library Director

The Cabot School District ranks 5th in the state for the number of National Board

School Board Recognition Month – Dr. Thurman and administrators thanked the school
board members for their dedication and hard work to our students, faculty, and
community.
CURRICULUM REPORT
One Book, One School – Stagecoach Elementary Principal Pam Wilson brought two
students, Allie and Levi, to present on their One Book, One School program. All
students at Stagecoach read Charlotte’s Web by E.B. White and were able to meet to
meet the goose and Wilbur the pig. Allie and Levi shared their favorite parts of the
book and what they liked best about One Book, One School.
ACSIP Pilot Program – Melanie Duerkop reported that we are one of 37 schools in
Arkansas participating in the ACSIP Pilot Program. ACSIP was previously focused on
scores and the plan to increase scores on a yearly basis. Indistar is the new program
and is focused on processes and practices, rather than just test scores. Indistar looks at
school strengths and how they can build on those strengths with a plan for continuous
improvement that does not end each year. Every school must have a leadership team
that meets at least twice a month to work on the indicators each school selects.
After School Programs – Michele French reported that Non-Title I schools will begin
their after school programs. They will be held twice a week for one hour after school for
a total of 16 sessions. Each school will have four teacher s for their program, and 200225 students will be served in these after school programs.
SUPERINTENDENT’S REPORT
Buildings and Grounds – Dr. Harold Jeffcoat shared that the water leak under the S
Building has been located and that water line will be rerouted in order to fix the
problem. Two projects coming up this summer are the second phase of the HVAC
system at Northside Elementary and replacing flooring at Middle School South.
Current Enrollment – For information only.
Legislative Update – Dr. Thurman shared a list of legislation that will be addressed in
the 2015 legislative session.
Cabot Panther Foundation – Brian Evans reported that Liz Massey was the speaker at
the last Foundation meeting and shared about the new Cabot Schools app. The

Foundation has been recognizing Real Proud, Real Panthers and Power Panthers at
sporting events. The following are some upcoming Foundation events:
A Daughter’s Heart Dance – February 19
Dancing with the Cabot Stars – March 31
CPF Golf Tournament – May 4
ACTION
The board voted to approve a resolution to pay dues to the Cabot and Ward Chambers
of Commerce in order to have full benefits with the chambers.
The board voted to approve the legal transfer of student D.A.
The board voted to uphold the administration’s recommendation to expel a student.
See your building administrator or supervisor for additional information.
The meeting adjourned at 7:55 p.m.

The Cabot City Council held its monthly Agenda Meeting on February 2, 2015 in the City Annex Council
Chambers. Council members present were: Ann Gilliam, Ed Long, Doyle Tullos, Dallan Buchanan, Ronald
Waymack, Kevin Davis, Jon Moore and Rick Prentice. Others present: Mayor Cypert, City Attorney Jim Taylor,
City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom, Calvin Aldridge, CPA, & Eddie Cook.

Ed Long, Chairman of the Public Works Committee called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.
Public Works:

1.

School Livestock Ordinance — Mike Wheeler introduced this information stating it was specific to the
school’s address only and without it the school is out of compliance with the city’s animal control
ordinance. The ordinance for Animal Husba ndry for Educational Purposes follows our current
ordinance. timmy Taylor recommended this to be a standalone ordinance. Discussion. Two
representatives from Cabot Public Schools, Monica Griffin & Corey Ruff addressed the council members
and answered questions. Discussion. After a member of the public asked about the smell and waste,
Monica Griffin reported to the council members that the school had contracted with a local farm to
accept clean up. The schoot will dump waste from sealed containers once a week and use cleanliness
as a major education point as it is their utmost priority. Corey Ruff reminded the council members that
their concerns are the schools as well. It is their campus and they want to keep it in great condition,
smelling good and looking great, they want their neighbors happy as well. The schools administration
recommends this program. Rick Prentice asked what the definition of temporary was, and stated he
liked the program but would like to see the dates the animals are allowed to be housed overnight
included in the legislation. Because of this, Ann made a motion to table this until the March Agenda
Meeting to give Jimmy time to work with the school on the dates that goats and lambs will be allowed
to be housed overnight. Second by Rick. Motion passed with a vote of 8-0.

Benefits
Line of Duty Death Premiums

For all full-time employees employed by the City and enrolled in the City’s primary health
insurance plan, if an employee dies in the line of duty, the City will pay the employee and the
employer’s portion of the insurance for up to 3 years for all eligible dependents who are covered
under the plan as dependents at the time the employee is killed in the line of duty. This does not
apply to “extra” or supplemental!” polices.

Line of duty death will be defined as:

Injuries resulting in death that occur while the employee is being paid for time worked
and the employee is acting in the capacity of a City employee and performing official job
duties that he or she would normally or reasonably perform.

Exclusion to this policy will happen when death occurs as a result of:

* While the employce is going to or from work and the event that causes death has nothing
to do with the employee’s job or job tasks.

¢ Self-inflicted injuries or intentional injuries that lead to death.

Any alcohol or drug related incident

e A result of natural causes including heart attack, stroke or disease, including if a natural
cause occurs while an employee is performing his or her normal job duties or tasks.

e Asaresult of injuries received more than one year before the date of the employee’s
death, unless before the expiration of five years from the date of the injury, the
dependents provide medical proof acceptable to the City that death was due to an injury
that occurred in the line of duty.

As stated, eligible dependents will be able to receive the insurance completely paid by the City
for up to 3 years. The following will result in the City no longer paying the full premium prior to
the end of 3 years:

e The dependents enroll in another group policy or plan. Once the dependents leave the
City’s plan, they are not allowed to return to the plan.

¢ lfachild dependent reaches the limiting age as stated in the plan.

¢ Ifthe City no longer provides health insurance to employees. (This does not include if the
City merely switches providers which the City reserves the right to do)

At any point the dependents come off of the insurance for any of the reasons listed above or 3

years pass, the dependents will be sent a COBRA notice and if eligible, they can continue to pay
the full premium for a specified amount of time.

Effective Date of Benefit: July 1, 2015 Exhibit “A”

Benefits

Tri-Care

Beginning in 2016, as allowed by law, all full time employees enrolled in Tri-Care single or
family coverage as a result of active or previous duty in the United States Military, the City
agrees to pay the full portion of the Tri-Care premium.

To take advantage of this, the employee must notify Human Resources at yearly open enrollment
so it can be accounted for in the following year’s budget. Exceptions will be made for new hires.

The City will only pay for the premium quarterly. Employees are to bring their bill to the Human
Resources Office cach quarter. The City does not accept responsibility if the bill is turned in late
to the City. In the event an employee terminates employment within that quarter, the payment
will be pro-rated and the employce will have to reimburse the City.

Effective Date of Benefit: January 1, 2016 EXHIBIT “B”
